chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Mufazzal who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you see a dispute between two from our Shia, so redeem it from my wealth'.

key_terms.شِيعَتِنَا: Our Shia (the followers of the Imams)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to 'redeem' a dispute between Shia according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs his followers to resolve disputes among themselves by 'redeeming' them, likely through financial compensation or settlement paid from the Imam's wealth, emphasizing the importance of unity and the Imam's role in maintaining social harmony within the community. This directive highlights the concept of *al-fidyah* (ransom/redeeming) in interpersonal conflicts, reflecting the Imam's spiritual and material authority in preserving the cohesion of the Shia community during the era of the Minor and Major Ghaibah. It underscores the practical application of unity (*tawhid* in social relations) as a means of earning divine pleasure and avoiding division.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Mufazzal who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you see a dispute between two from our<sup>asws</sup> Shia, so redeem it from my<sup>asws</sup> wealth’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Sinan from Mufaddal who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘When you find two of our followers disputing, settle it between them by means of paying from my property.’”
